claim: There is consistently a graph of chromatic number aleph-2 all of whose triangle-free subgraphs have chromatic number at most aleph-1; under CH such a graph, if K4-free, is not a countable union of triangle-free graphs and answers Erdos problem 595.
domain: infinite graph theory / set theory / partition calculus

facets.entities: infinite graphs of uncountable chromatic number and their triangle-free or high-girth subgraphs
facets.mechanism: a chromatic gap between a graph and its triangle-free subgraphs, forced by a set-theoretic construction
facets.method: Rodl subgraph theorem, Erdos-Hajnal partition calculus, Hajnal consistency constructions, Todorcevic walks on ordinals, forcing and negative square-bracket partition relations
facets.outcome: existence or consistency of a graph whose triangle-free subgraphs all have strictly smaller chromatic number than the graph
